study_identification_part.si_3_author_journal_year: Coupé et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2022
study_identification_part.si_4_title: Hippocampal-amygdalo-ventricular atrophy score: Alzheimer disease detection using normative and pathological lifespan models

nm2_1_modeling_methods.detail: Polynomial regression (Linear, Quadratic, Cubic) selected via BIC.
nm2_1_modeling_methods.supporting_text: To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: Linear model, Quadratic model, Cubic model

nm2_2_response_variable.detail: The study modeled trajectories for 132 structures, including gray matter, white matter, CSF, and subcortical structures. Key discriminant structures identified were hippocampus, amygdala, and inferior lateral ventricle.
nm2_2_response_variable.supporting_text: the brain was segmented into several structures... These structures are combined to create tissue segmentations (gray matter [GM], white matter [WM], and cerebrospinal fluid [CSF]), regional tissue segmentations... and lobar segmentations... we selected all the multiscale brain areas... for which CN and AD models significantly diverged... amygdala, hippocampus, and inferior lateral ventricle were the most discriminant structures

nm2_3_explanatory_variables.detail: Polynomial models of age (Linear, Quadratic, Cubic) were used.
nm2_3_explanatory_variables.supporting_text: To estimate the volume trajectories, we considered several low order polynomial models: Linear model, Quadratic model, Cubic model
